summary: Wall Street's AI sell-off deepened: the S&P 500 fell 2% on Thursday for a sixth straight loss and the Dow dropped 1,101 points, with Nvidia down about another 6.7% in Friday morning trade.

Russia launched one of the largest attacks of the war on Ukraine, firing over 400 drones and 110 missiles, killing at least six in Kyiv and damaging Dnipro bridges, while an unidentified object fell in eastern Poland.
The NZX 50 fell 1% on Friday, ending three straight weekly gains, while the national average for 91 petrol eased to about $3.25 a litre.

stories.headline: AI sell-off drags Wall Street to a sixth straight loss
stories.summary: The S&P 500 fell 2% to 7,175.83 on Thursday, its longest losing streak since 2024 and 8.2% below last month's record, while the Dow lost 1,101 points to 49,097.06. More than 90% of S&P 500 stocks fell as worries grew that the AI boom may be fading, even as Anthropic closed its first day at US$97.17, above its US$83 IPO price.
stories.why: US tech shares make up a big slice of most KiwiSaver growth funds, so a week like this shows up in your balance.

stories.headline: NZX 50 snaps a three-week winning run
stories.summary: The NZX 50 fell 139.84 points, or 1%, to 14,107.41 on Friday, leaving it down 0.5% for the week after hitting a record 14,352.72 on Tuesday. a2 Milk lost 13% over the week after cutting its revenue guidance, while Serko gained 11%.
stories.why: The local market had held up well, but global AI jitters are now reaching NZ shares, which matters for NZ-heavy KiwiSaver funds.

nz_politics.headline: Major parties' combined vote hits an MMP low
nz_politics.summary: Analysis by The Post's Henry Cooke found only 62% of party votes went to National or Labour, the lowest share in MMP history. Opportunity won 12.8% in Wellington, more than double its national result, while the official count including special votes is due on 27 November.
nz_politics.why: A Parliament with more minor-party votes usually means more negotiated policy on tax, KiwiSaver and small-business rules.

nz_politics.headline: Shane Jones sets out mining demands before talks
nz_politics.summary: Caretaker Resources Minister Shane Jones wants the 1953 Wildlife Act rewritten and DOC's say over commercial mining and development permits removed, raising it ahead of coalition talks. DOC has reversed its refusal of a Macraes mine expansion permit after Jones warned 700 jobs were at risk.
nz_politics.why: How permits and environmental rules are handled is an early marker of the business settings the next government may adopt.

world.headline: Russia hits Kyiv in one of the war's largest attacks
world.summary: Ukraine says Russia fired more than 400 drones and over 110 missiles overnight, killing at least six people in Kyiv and two at a Lviv train station. Three bridges over the Dnipro were hit, with the Podil-Voskresensky crossing closed to traffic heading to the left bank.
world.why: Escalation in Ukraine keeps pressure on global energy prices, which flow through to NZ fuel and inflation.

world.headline: Object crashes in eastern Poland during Russian strikes
world.summary: An unidentified object fell near the village of Chmielek in Poland's Lublin region and caught fire, with no casualties reported, as Russia struck western Ukraine. Prime Minister Donald Tusk convened ministers, military chiefs and intelligence heads over the airspace violation, and Polish air defences were put on alert.
world.why: Any spillover onto NATO territory raises the risk of wider conflict, which moves markets and the Kiwi dollar.

stories.headline: Breman says fuel and a weak Kiwi keep inflation high
stories.summary: Reserve Bank Governor Anna Breman told an Institute of Directors event in Auckland that inflation remains above the 2% midpoint, pushed by fuel costs and a weaker New Zealand dollar, while the recovery is uneven. She said the Monetary Policy Committee will weigh the data and act as needed before its next decision.
stories.why: Her tone feeds into whether the OCR rises in December, which would make vehicle and equipment loans dearer.

stories.headline: Pump prices keep sliding from October's peak
stories.summary: The national average for 91 was $3.25 a litre on 19 November, down 27.4 cents over 28 days, with diesel at about $2.96, according to Gaspy data from more than 1,500 stations. Stats NZ figures show petrol was still 38% dearer in October than a year earlier.
stories.why: Cheaper fuel directly lowers the cost of driving between jobs, so it's a good moment to check your quote prices still cover travel.

marketing.headline: Coca-Cola drops AI for live-action Christmas films
marketing.summary: Coca-Cola's 2026 'Enjoy Joy' holiday campaign, running in the US from 19 November, uses live-action films after its AI-generated ads in 2024 and 2025 drew criticism. It comes in 30-, 15- and 6-second cuts for TV, streaming and social, backed by creator content on Meta, TikTok, Pinterest and YouTube.
marketing.why: Even giant brands are finding people respond better to real footage, so genuine before-and-after clips of your own jobs beat stock or AI imagery.

marketing.headline: Google Ads switches on more AI by default
marketing.summary: Google Ads Editor 2.14 now turns on AI Max, text asset automation and final URL expansion by default for new Search campaigns built in Editor. Google also lets advertisers download their Local Services Ads history ahead of those ads moving into Google Ads.
marketing.why: If you run Google ads for Coastal Clear Windows, check new campaigns so Google isn't rewriting your ads or sending clicks to pages you didn't choose.

term.definition: A fall of 10% or more from a recent high in a share index or stock. It's bigger than a normal dip but smaller than a bear market (a 20% fall), and corrections happen fairly often.
term.example: After losing 6.2% this week, the Dow is just under 10% below its record, while the S&P 500 sits 8.2% below its peak.
